/-!
# Jaeger's Petersen-coloring conjecture

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Petersen graph: Petersen coloring conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petersen_graph%23Petersen_coloring_conjecture)
- [Ja88] Jaeger, F., *Nowhere-zero flow problems*. In: Selected Topics in Graph Theory 3,
  Academic Press (1988), 71--95.

An *Eulerian subgraph* of a graph $G$ is a set of edges of $G$ meeting every vertex of $G$ an
even number of times. These edge sets are the elements of the cycle space of $G$ over
$\mathbb{Z}/2$ and are also called *cycles*. A map from the edges of $G$ to the edges of $H$ is
*cycle-continuous* if the preimage of every cycle of $H$ is a cycle of $G$.

Jaeger's Petersen-coloring conjecture asserts that every bridgeless cubic graph has a
cycle-continuous mapping to the Petersen graph. The Wikipedia article on the Petersen graph
states the conjecture for all bridgeless graphs; that version is known to be equivalent to the
cubic one, which is the form posed by the list entry and formalised here.
-/
open SimpleGraph
namespace JaegersPetersenColoringConjecture
variable {V W : Type*}

two-element subsets of a five-element set, and two of them are adjacent if and only if they are
disjoint. -/

def IsEvenSubgraph [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (C : Set G.edgeSet) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : V, Even {e ∈ C | v ∈ (e : Sym2 V)}.ncard
blocks.docstring:
A set `C` of edges of `G` is an *even subgraph* (an *Eulerian subgraph*, or a *cycle* in the
sense of the cycle space over $\mathbb{Z}/2$) if every vertex of `G` lies on an even number of
edges of `C`. Connectedness is not required. The finiteness assumption on the vertex type makes
`Set.ncard` count the edges of `C` at a vertex correctly.

justification.closest_existing_considered: SimpleGraph.Walk.IsEulerian (Mathlib), SimpleGraph.Cycle (FormalConjecturesForMathlib), SimpleGraph.incidenceSet/degree (used in the API lemma checking the definition).
justification.name: JaegersPetersenColoringConjecture.IsEvenSubgraph
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of the Z/2 cycle space or of even/Eulerian edge subsets of a SimpleGraph; `SimpleGraph.Walk.IsEulerian` is about trails and requires a single closed walk, and `SimpleGraph.Cycle` (repo) is a single cycle walk, neither of which matches 'edge set meeting every vertex evenly'.

blocks.name: IsEvenSubgraph
blocks.text:
/-- A set `C` of edges of `G` is an *even subgraph* (an *Eulerian subgraph*, or a *cycle* in the
sense of the cycle space over $\mathbb{Z}/2$) if every vertex of `G` lies on an even number of
edges of `C`. Connectedness is not required. The finiteness assumption on the vertex type makes
`Set.ncard` count the edges of `C` at a vertex correctly. -/
def IsEvenSubgraph [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (C : Set G.edgeSet) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : V, Even {e ∈ C | v ∈ (e : Sym2 V)}.ncard

blocks.docstring:
A map `f` from the edges of `G` to the edges of `H` is *cycle-continuous* if the preimage
under `f` of every even subgraph (cycle) of `H` is an even subgraph (cycle) of `G`. No
compatibility with the vertices is required: `f` is merely a map between edge sets.

justification.closest_existing_considered: SimpleGraph.Hom (graph homomorphism) — explicitly not what the statement requires, since the map is only on edges with no vertex compatibility.
justification.name: JaegersPetersenColoringConjecture.IsCycleContinuous
justification.why_needed: Cycle-continuous maps between edge sets do not exist in Mathlib or the repo (searched for cycleSpace, cycle-continuous, IsEulerian).

blocks.name: IsCycleContinuous
blocks.text:
/-- A map `f` from the edges of `G` to the edges of `H` is *cycle-continuous* if the preimage
under `f` of every even subgraph (cycle) of `H` is an even subgraph (cycle) of `G`. No
compatibility with the vertices is required: `f` is merely a map between edge sets. -/
def IsCycleContinuous [Finite V] [Finite W] {G : SimpleGraph V} {H : SimpleGraph W}
    (f : G.edgeSet → H.edgeSet) : Prop :=
  ∀ C : Set H.edgeSet, IsEvenSubgraph H C → IsEvenSubgraph G (f ⁻¹' C)

blocks.docstring:
**Jaeger's Petersen-coloring conjecture.** Every bridgeless cubic graph has a cycle-continuous
mapping to the Petersen graph.

Here a *cubic graph* is a finite simple graph in which every vertex has degree $3$
(connectedness is not required), a graph is *bridgeless* if none of its edges is a bridge, and a
map $f \colon E(G) \to E(P)$ to the edge set of the Petersen graph $P$ is *cycle-continuous* if the
preimage under $f$ of every cycle (Eulerian subgraph) of $P$ is a cycle of $G$.

theorem ncard_univ_incident [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (v : V) : {e ∈ (Set.univ : Set G.edgeSet) | v ∈ (e : Sym2 V)}.ncard = G.degree v := by
  have h : Subtype.val '' {e ∈ (Set.univ : Set G.edgeSet) | v ∈ (e : Sym2 V)} =
      G.incidenceSet v := by
    ext e
    simp [incidenceSet, and_comm]
  rw [← Set.ncard_image_of_injective _ Subtype.val_injective, h, Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card',
    ← incidenceFinset, card_incidenceFinset_eq_degree]

/-- The composite of two cycle-continuous maps is cycle-continuous. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsCycleContinuous.comp {U : Type*} [Finite U] [Finite V] [Finite W]
    {G : SimpleGraph U} {H : SimpleGraph V} {K : SimpleGraph W}
    {g : H.edgeSet → K.edgeSet} {f : G.edgeSet → H.edgeSet}
    (hg : IsCycleContinuous g) (hf : IsCycleContinuous f) : IsCycleContinuous (g ∘ f) :=
  fun C hC => hf _ (hg C hC)
end JaegersPetersenColoringConjecture

claims.decomposer_note: Single universally quantified Prop over finite (simple) 3-regular graphs with no bridge (connectedness not required); a cycle-continuous mapping is a function f : E(G) → E(Petersen) such that the preimage of every cycle (Eulerian subgraph / element of the Z/2 cycle space, i.e. edge set meeting every vertex evenly) of the Petersen graph is a cycle of G — a merely edge-set map, not a graph homomorphism; the article states the conjecture for all bridgeless graphs, which is known to be equivalent to this cubic form, but the statement only poses the cubic version, so no variant slot is added.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates compile and are mathematically equivalent faithful statements: finite simple graph (SimpleGraph V, [Fintype V]), cubic = IsRegularOfDegree 3, bridgeless = repo's SimpleGraph.IsBridgeless (no edge is a Mathlib IsBridge), no connectedness assumption, cycle = Z/2 cycle-space element (edge set meeting each vertex an even number of times), cycle-continuous = bare edge-set map f : G.edgeSet → P.edgeSet whose preimages of even edge sets are even edge sets, Petersen graph correct (I verified both the Kneser K(5,2) model and the Fin 10 pentagon/spokes/pentagram model satisfy srg(10,3,0,1), which characterises the Petersen graph). The statement is non-trivial: a constant map pulls a 5-cycle of P back to all of E(G), which is not even in a cubic graph; the empty graph case is trivially true, as in the informal statement. c06 chosen as base because its definitions carry [Finite V] so Set.ncard is a genuine count, its Petersen definition is certified by an srg(10,3,0,1) test plus 15-edge and bridgelessness tests, and it has API lemmas linking even subgraphs to degree. Edits: module docstring tightened (list entry cited first; general-bridgeless variant noted as equivalent, not formalised per the table), test lemma renamed to not_isEvenSubgraph_univ_petersenGraph.

context:
In the mathematical field of graph theory, the Petersen graph is an undirected graph with 10 vertices and 15 edges. It is a small graph that serves as a useful example and counterexample for many problems in graph theory. The Petersen graph is named after Julius Petersen, who in 1898 constructed it to be the smallest bridgeless cubic graph with no three-edge-coloring.
Although the graph is generally credited to Petersen, it had in fact first appeared 12 years earlier, in a paper by A. B. Kempe (1886). Kempe observed that its vertices can represent the ten lines of the Desargues configuration, and its edges represent pairs of lines that do not meet at one of the ten points of the configuration.
Donald Knuth states that the Petersen graph is "a remarkable configuration that serves as a counterexample to many optimistic predictions about what might be true for graphs in general."
The Petersen graph also makes an appearance in tropical geometry. The cone over the Petersen graph is naturally identified with the moduli space of five-pointed rational tropical curves.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The table's reading (single universally quantified Prop over finite simple bridgeless cubic graphs, cycle-continuous map as a bare edge-set map with the Z/2 cycle-space notion of cycle, no variant slot for general bridgeless graphs) matches the Wikipedia list entry and the linked Petersen graph article, and was followed exactly.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Jaeger's Petersen-coloring conjecture

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Petersen graph: Petersen coloring conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petersen_graph%23Petersen_coloring_conjecture)
- [Ja88] Jaeger, F., *Nowhere-zero flow problems*. In: Selected Topics in Graph Theory 3,
  Academic Press (1988), 71--95.

An *Eulerian subgraph* of a graph $G$ is a set of edges of $G$ meeting every vertex of $G$ an
even number of times. These edge sets are the elements of the cycle space of $G$ over
$\mathbb{Z}/2$ and are also called *cycles*. A map from the edges of $G$ to the edges of $H$ is
*cycle-continuous* if the preimage of every cycle of $H$ is a cycle of $G$.

Jaeger's Petersen-coloring conjecture asserts that every bridgeless cubic graph has a
cycle-continuous mapping to the Petersen graph. The Wikipedia article on the Petersen graph
states the conjecture for all bridgeless graphs; that version is known to be equivalent to the
cubic one, which is the form posed by the list entry and formalised here.
-/

open SimpleGraph

namespace JaegersPetersenColoringConjecture

variable {V W : Type*}

/-- The Petersen graph, realised as the Kneser graph $KG(5, 2)$: its vertices are the $10$
two-element subsets of a five-element set, and two of them are adjacent if and only if they are
disjoint. -/
def petersenGraph : SimpleGraph {s : Finset (Fin 5) // s.card = 2} where
  Adj s t := Disjoint s.1 t.1
  symm _ _ h := h.symm
  loopless s h := by
    have hs := s.2
    simp only [Finset.disjoint_self_iff_empty] at h
    simp [h] at hs

instance : DecidableRel petersenGraph.Adj :=
  fun s t => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (Disjoint s.1 t.1))

/-- A set `C` of edges of `G` is an *even subgraph* (an *Eulerian subgraph*, or a *cycle* in the
sense of the cycle space over $\mathbb{Z}/2$) if every vertex of `G` lies on an even number of
edges of `C`. Connectedness is not required. The finiteness assumption on the vertex type makes
`Set.ncard` count the edges of `C` at a vertex correctly. -/
def IsEvenSubgraph [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (C : Set G.edgeSet) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : V, Even {e ∈ C | v ∈ (e : Sym2 V)}.ncard

/-- A map `f` from the edges of `G` to the edges of `H` is *cycle-continuous* if the preimage
under `f` of every even subgraph (cycle) of `H` is an even subgraph (cycle) of `G`. No
compatibility with the vertices is required: `f` is merely a map between edge sets. -/
def IsCycleContinuous [Finite V] [Finite W] {G : SimpleGraph V} {H : SimpleGraph W}
    (f : G.edgeSet → H.edgeSet) : Prop :=
  ∀ C : Set H.edgeSet, IsEvenSubgraph H C → IsEvenSubgraph G (f ⁻¹' C)

/--
**Jaeger's Petersen-coloring conjecture.** Every bridgeless cubic graph has a cycle-continuous
mapping to the Petersen graph.

Here a *cubic graph* is a finite simple graph in which every vertex has degree $3$
(connectedness is not required), a graph is *bridgeless* if none of its edges is a bridge, and a
map $f \colon E(G) \to E(P)$ to the edge set of the Petersen graph $P$ is *cycle-continuous* if the
preimage under $f$ of every cycle (Eulerian subgraph) of $P$ is a cycle of $G$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem jaegers_petersen_coloring_conjecture [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hcubic : G.IsRegularOfDegree 3) (hbridgeless : G.IsBridgeless) :
    ∃ f : G.edgeSet → petersenGraph.edgeSet, IsCycleContinuous f := by
  sorry

/-- The Petersen graph is the (unique) strongly regular graph with parameters $(10, 3, 0, 1)$: it
has $10$ vertices, is cubic, adjacent vertices have no common neighbour and non-adjacent vertices
have exactly one common neighbour. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem petersenGraph_isSRGWith : petersenGraph.IsSRGWith 10 3 0 1 where
  card := by
    rw [Fintype.card_finset_len, Fintype.card_fin]
    rfl
  regular := by
    unfold IsRegularOfDegree
    decide
  of_adj := by decide
  of_not_adj := by
    unfold Pairwise
    decide

/-- The Petersen graph has $15$ edges. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem card_petersenGraph_edgeFinset : petersenGraph.edgeFinset.card = 15 := by
  decide

/-- The Petersen graph is bridgeless. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem petersenGraph_isBridgeless : petersenGraph.IsBridgeless := by
  intro e he
  induction e using Sym2.ind with
  | h u v =>
    rw [isBridge_iff]
    revert u v
    decide

/-- The empty set of edges is an even subgraph. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isEvenSubgraph_empty [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsEvenSubgraph G ∅ := by
  intro v
  simp

/-- The number of edges of `G` at a vertex `v` is the degree of `v`. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem ncard_univ_incident [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (v : V) : {e ∈ (Set.univ : Set G.edgeSet) | v ∈ (e : Sym2 V)}.ncard = G.degree v := by
  have h : Subtype.val '' {e ∈ (Set.univ : Set G.edgeSet) | v ∈ (e : Sym2 V)} =
      G.incidenceSet v := by
    ext e
    simp [incidenceSet, and_comm]
  rw [← Set.ncard_image_of_injective _ Subtype.val_injective, h, Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card',
    ← incidenceFinset, card_incidenceFinset_eq_degree]

/-- The whole edge set of `G` is an even subgraph if and only if every vertex has even degree. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isEvenSubgraph_univ_iff [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] : IsEvenSubgraph G Set.univ ↔ ∀ v, Even (G.degree v) := by
  simp only [IsEvenSubgraph, ncard_univ_incident]

/-- The whole edge set of the Petersen graph is not a cycle, since every vertex has degree $3$. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isEvenSubgraph_univ_petersenGraph : ¬ IsEvenSubgraph petersenGraph Set.univ := by
  rw [isEvenSubgraph_univ_iff]
  decide

/-- The identity map on the edges of a graph is cycle-continuous. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isCycleContinuous_id [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) :
    IsCycleContinuous (id : G.edgeSet → G.edgeSet) :=
  fun _ hC => hC

/-- The composite of two cycle-continuous maps is cycle-continuous. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsCycleContinuous.comp {U : Type*} [Finite U] [Finite V] [Finite W]
    {G : SimpleGraph U} {H : SimpleGraph V} {K : SimpleGraph W}
    {g : H.edgeSet → K.edgeSet} {f : G.edgeSet → H.edgeSet}
    (hg : IsCycleContinuous g) (hf : IsCycleContinuous f) : IsCycleContinuous (g ∘ f) :=
  fun C hC => hf _ (hg C hC)

end JaegersPetersenColoringConjecture

items: Cubic graphs are taken to be finite *simple* 3-regular graphs (`SimpleGraph V` with `[Fintype V]` and `G.IsRegularOfDegree 3`), as prescribed by the decomposition notes; Jaeger's original conjecture and much of the literature allow cubic multigraphs (parallel edges), but the simple-graph version is the one the table asks for and is known to be equivalent. Connectedness is not required.
Bridgeless uses the existing repo definition `SimpleGraph.IsBridgeless` (∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, ¬ G.IsBridge e) from FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Cycle.lean.

A 'cycle' of a graph (in the cycle-continuity sense) is formalized as `IsEvenSubgraph G C` for `C : Set G.edgeSet`: for every vertex v, the number (`Set.ncard`) of edges of C containing v is even. This is exactly the article's 'Eulerian subgraph / element of the Z/2 cycle space'; connectedness is not required. The definition carries an (otherwise unused) `[Finite V]` hypothesis so that `Set.ncard` is a genuine count; an API lemma `isEvenSubgraph_univ_iff` checks it against `SimpleGraph.degree`.

A cycle-continuous mapping is a bare function `f : G.edgeSet → H.edgeSet` between edge subtypes (no vertex compatibility / not a graph homomorphism) such that `f ⁻¹' C` is an even subgraph of G whenever C is an even subgraph of H. Preimage is `Set.preimage` on `Set H.edgeSet`.

The Petersen graph is defined as the Kneser graph KG(5,2): vertices are `{s : Finset (Fin 5) // s.card = 2}`, adjacency is `Disjoint`. Its correctness is certified by the test `petersenGraph_isSRGWith : petersenGraph.IsSRGWith 10 3 0 1` (the Petersen graph is the unique srg(10,3,0,1)), plus 15 edges and bridgelessness, all proved by kernel `decide`.

The empty vertex type satisfies the hypotheses vacuously and the conclusion holds trivially (empty edge set), so there is no degenerate-case defect. No variant for general (non-cubic) bridgeless graphs was added, per the decomposition notes.

reviewer_notes: Single-slot problem; no candidate omitted the slot and no omission reasons to weigh. Modeling caveats (shared by all candidates and fixed by the decomposition table): graphs are finite simple graphs, so cubic multigraphs with parallel edges (allowed in some literature statements of Jaeger's conjecture) are excluded; the Wikipedia list entry says 'graph', and the simple cubic form is known to be equivalent to the general one. Cycles are taken as Eulerian edge sets (Z/2 cycle space), exactly as the linked Petersen-graph article defines them; using circuits instead would give an equivalent notion of cycle-continuity. c05's report claims the Fin 10 Petersen model is 'already used elsewhere in the repository' — false (no Petersen graph exists in the repo), but harmless. Bespoke definitions (petersenGraph, IsEvenSubgraph, IsCycleContinuous) are kept in the problem file; a maintainer may wish to move petersenGraph to FormalConjecturesForMathlib as a reusable definition.
